place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 外门 · 饭堂门口
place.en: Chending Temple · The outer court · the refectory door

setup.zh: 九月初十，天没亮，饭堂门口排起了长龙：周衡发腰牌、灵石，马小宝收公中。身后有人拍你肩膀——阿禾。
setup.en: The tenth of the ninth month, before dawn, a long queue at the refectory door: Zhou Heng hands out waist tags and spirit stones, Ma Xiaobao collects the common fund. Someone taps your shoulder from behind — Ah He.

recap.zh: 入门第二天，阿禾也在——考进来的，三灵根，「中上之资」；她在小本子上记了你一笔：下下之资，利息以后再算。
recap.en: Your second day in the sect, Ah He was there too — passed on merit, three roots, "above the middle"; she wrote you into her notebook: bottom of the bottom, interest reckoned later.

zh: 九月初十，饭堂门口，领灵石，交公中。
身后有人拍你的肩膀——一个红鼻头。
en: The tenth of the ninth month, the refectory door: draw stones, pay the common fund.
Someone taps your shoulder — a red nose.

story.zh:
沉鼎山外门的日子，沈小满是从交钱开始过的——钱还没捂热，便有人伸手来收。九月初十，天还没亮透，饭堂门口便排起了长龙。一百来个新弟子，穿着昨夜才领的灰袍，袍子是照着大个子裁的，小个子穿上，下摆拖到脚面，远远看过去，倒像一群刚出窝的灰鸭子。

饭堂门口摆一张榆木桌子，桌子后面坐着外门执事周衡。周衡是个三十来岁的瘦高个儿，一脸愁苦，面前摊着一本厚得能当枕头使的账簿，叫一个名字，发一块枣木腰牌，三块灵石。那灵石有鸽子蛋大小，灰扑扑的，里头却隐隐透出一点光来，像雪地里埋着的一粒火星。周衡发一个人，便抬头看那人一眼，道一声：「有前途！」发到第三十几个，那三个字已经说得像念经。轮到小满，他看了看名册上「五行杂灵根」那几个字，端详了小满好一会儿，道：「……有前途。」没有那个叹号。

进了饭堂的门，往前走不上十步，又是一张桌子。桌子后面坐着马小宝，面前摆一只描金的小木匣，匣上贴一张红纸，写着两个大字：**公中**。他身后站着两个进门三年的老弟子，抱着胳膊，像庙门口的两尊泥塑。唱名的那个执事——河滩上冲白衣人点头、正殿里替马小宝添了一道的那一个——是马三的表哥，马小宝的表伯；一夜之间，马小宝便成了「马师兄」。排在小满前头的孙二狗，背上还背着那个比他身子还大的包袱，捧着三块灵石看了半天，拣出最小的一块，哆哆嗦嗦地放进了匣子。他刚要走，身后那尊泥塑伸出一条腿来，在他脚后跟上一勾，他背着那个大包袱往前一栽，脚下踉跄了三四步，歪歪斜斜，像一根给风吹弯了的芦苇，弯到了地皮上，偏偏又弹了回来——竟没有倒。

小满拣了一块不大不小的，放进匣子里。马小宝眯起眼睛：「就这么交了？」小满道：「规矩嘛。小宝哥辛苦。」马小宝道：「叫马师兄。」小满道：「马师兄辛苦。」马小宝满意地一扬下巴，腰上一块旧木牌晃了一晃，一面刻着「巡夜」两个字——外门最松快的差事，他表伯顺手派给了他。小满凑得近，鼻子里忽然钻进一股味儿：不是桂花糕的甜，是一股青苦的草腥气，凉丝丝的，吸进去，肚子底下那口枯井，竟像是给凉水激了一下。马小宝一夜巡回来，身上带的就是这个。

小满往前走了十步，摸出娘给的那个红糖包纸订的本子，翻过头一页「石蛋」「小豆。太华。」那两行，舔了舔笔尖：**九月初十。公中。灵石一块。马小宝。**

身后忽然有人拍他肩膀。

小满回头一看，是一个扎两根小辫子的姑娘，灰袍比他的还大一号，袖子挽了三道，下摆拿草绳在腰里扎了一圈。一个红鼻头，冻得像一根萝卜。手里捏着一个巴掌大的小本子，一截炭条夹在耳朵上。

小满道：「……阿禾。你躲了我一整天。」

阿禾道：「嗯。」

「你怎么来的？」

「考进来的。」阿禾道，「石阶上，我从你边上冲过去的。洛书，我比你先摆好半炷香。」她顿了一顿，一本正经地道，「考试的时候，不认人。认了你，要分心。」小满道：「那现在呢？」阿禾道：「现在考完了。」

她把小本子翻开来给他看。前一页是昨天的，炭条字一行一行：

九月初九。重阳。

九个数。没人教我口诀。一到九，加一遍，四十五。分三份，十五。先算总数，再摆。

林子。我闭着眼睛进去的。看了要记，记了要怕。不看。

马家的人往林子里扔了一颗石子。我看见了。葛镖头也看见了。名册上写的是「自失」。记。

石蛋。十二。

禾种三十粒，缝在袄里。

翻过一页，是刚写的一行：**九月初十。他喊我，两回半。**小满问：「半回是什么？」阿禾道：「正殿里，你张了嘴，没敢喊，算半回。」小满没话说了，只好换个问题：「你怎么没跟我一起来？」

阿禾道：「我娘说，你一个人去，会死。我一个人去，也会死。两个人一起去，死一双，不划算。所以分开走。」小满想了一想，觉得这话虽然难听，账倒是算得明白。阿禾舔了舔炭条，又写了一行，念道：「『九月初十。沈小满。下下之资。』利息，以后再算。」
story.en:
Shen Xiaoman's days in the outer court of Mount Chending began with paying money — before the money was even warm, someone held out a hand for it. The tenth of the ninth month, before it was properly light, a long line had already formed at the refectory door. A hundred-odd new disciples in the grey robes handed out only last night — robes cut for big boys, so on the small ones the hems trailed on their feet; seen from a distance they looked like a brood of grey ducklings just out of the nest.

At the refectory door stood an elm table, and behind it sat the outer-court steward Zhou Heng — a tall thin man of thirty or so with a careworn face, before him a ledger thick enough to sleep on. He called a name and handed out a jujube-wood waist token and three spirit stones. The stones were the size of a pigeon's egg, dull grey, yet a faint light showed inside, like a spark buried in snow. With each one he looked up at the disciple and said: "Promising!" By the thirtieth-odd the word had become a chant. When it was Xiaoman's turn he looked at "five-element mixed root" in the register and studied Xiaoman a long while. "…Promising." Without the exclamation mark.

Inside the refectory door, not ten steps on, was another table. Behind it sat Ma Xiaobao with a little gilt box in front of him, a strip of red paper pasted on it bearing two big characters: **COMMON FUND**. Behind him stood two old disciples three years in, arms folded, like the clay guardians at a temple gate. The roll-calling steward — the one who had nodded to the man in white on the flats, and who had added Ma Xiaobao's missing stroke himself in the main hall — was Ma San's elder cousin — Ma Xiaobao's uncle; overnight Ma Xiaobao had become "Senior Brother Ma." Ahead of Xiaoman was Sun Ergou, still carrying that bundle bigger than himself; he held his three stones and looked at them a long while, picked out the smallest, and set it trembling in the box. He was just moving off when one of the clay guardians stuck out a leg and hooked his heel; with the big bundle on his back he pitched forward, staggered three or four steps, swaying every which way, like a reed blown flat by the wind, bent right down to the ground — and sprang back up. He didn't fall.

Xiaoman chose one neither big nor small and put it in the box. Ma Xiaobao narrowed his eyes. "Just like that?" Xiaoman said, "Rules are rules. Thank you for your trouble, Brother Xiaobao." Ma Xiaobao said, "Senior Brother Ma." Xiaoman said, "Thank you for your trouble, Senior Brother Ma." Ma Xiaobao lifted his chin, satisfied, and an old wooden token swung at his waist, one face carved NIGHT WATCH — the easiest post in the outer court, which his uncle had tossed him. Xiaoman was close, and a smell slipped into his nose: not the sweetness of osmanthus cake but a green, bitter, grassy smell, cool; breathing it in, the dry well beneath his belly seemed splashed with cold water. Ma Xiaobao came back from a night's watch carrying this on him.

Xiaoman walked ten steps on, took out the notebook his mother had stitched from brown-sugar paper, turned past the first page with its two lines, "Shidan" and "Xiaodou. Taihua.", licked the brush tip: **Tenth of the ninth. Common fund. One spirit stone. Ma Xiaobao.**

Someone tapped him on the shoulder from behind.

Xiaoman turned. It was a girl with two little braids, her grey robe a size bigger even than his, the sleeves rolled three times, the hem tied round her waist with straw rope. A red nose, frozen like a radish. In her hand a notebook no bigger than a palm; a stick of charcoal tucked behind her ear.

Xiaoman said, "…Ah He. You dodged me all day."

"Mm," said Ah He.

"How did you get here?"

"Got in," said Ah He. "On the stair, I ran past you. The Luo diagram, I finished half a stick of incense before you." She paused, and said very seriously, "In an exam you don't know anyone. Know you, and I'm distracted." Xiaoman said, "And now?" Ah He said, "Now the exam's over."

She opened the notebook to show him. The page before was yesterday's, in charcoal, line by line:

The ninth of the ninth. Double Ninth.

Nine numbers. Nobody taught me a rhyme. One to nine, added once: forty-five. Split three ways: fifteen. Reckon the total first, then set the stones.

The forest. I went in with my eyes shut. Look, and you remember; remember, and you're afraid. So don't look.

The Ma man threw a pebble into the forest. I saw. Escort Ge saw too. The register says "lost himself". Note it.

Shidan. Twelve.

Thirty grains of seed rice, sewn into my jacket.

She turned the page to the line she'd just written: **Tenth of the ninth. He called me two and a half times.** Xiaoman asked, "What's the half?" Ah He said, "In the hall you opened your mouth and didn't dare call. That's half." Xiaoman had nothing to say to that, so he changed the subject. "Why didn't you come with me?"

Ah He said, "My mum said, if you go alone you'll die. If I go alone I'll die too. If we go together, two die — bad bargain. So we went separately." Xiaoman thought it over: it sounded awful, but the sums were right. Ah He licked her charcoal and wrote another line, and read it out: "'Tenth of the ninth. Shen Xiaoman. Lowest of the low.' Interest to be reckoned later."

exits.means: accepts Ah He's entry, lets the interest stand, goes on to the lesson

what.zh: 外门第一天，阿禾在小本子上记了你一笔：下下之资。利息，以后再算。
what.en: Your first day in the outer court: Ah He wrote you into the little notebook — bottom of the class. Interest to be reckoned later.

story.zh:
小满想了一想，道：「记吧。利息，我认。」

阿禾点了点头，像是他总算说了一句像样的话。她转身要走，走了两步，又回过头来，补了一句：「鸡蛋，三个半。别忘了。」

小满站在原地，瞧着她那两截小辫子一跳一跳地走远了，心里头说不出是什么滋味。他想起出门那天，老槐树底下只站着他娘一个人。他那时候还道这丫头在睡懒觉。

原来她早走了一天，走的是另一条路。

那几天，小满逢人便问一句：太华山多远？孙二狗不知道。讲堂上一个老弟子听见了，笑他：「西边，两千来里，雍州。太华山上的太一宫，天下头一号的仙门。宫里的真传，身子金贵，碰破一块皮，有人替他挨板子。你问它做什么？」小满没说做什么。他翻开本子，在「小豆。太华。」后头，添了三个字：两千里。
story.en:
Xiaoman thought it over and said, "Write it down. The interest — I'll own it."

Ah He nodded, as if he had finally said something sensible. She turned to go, took two steps, looked back and added, "Eggs: three and a half. Don't forget."

Xiaoman stood where he was and watched her two little braids bob away, and could not have said what he felt. He remembered the day he left: under the old locust tree there had been only his mother. He had supposed the girl was sleeping in.

So she had gone a day early, by another road.

For the next few days Xiaoman asked everyone the same thing: how far is Mount Taihua? Sun Ergou didn't know. An older disciple in the lecture hall overheard and laughed at him. "West. Two thousand li and more, in Yongzhou. The Taiyi Palace, up on Mount Taihua — the first sect under heaven. Their true disciples are precious; graze one's skin and somebody else takes the beating for him. What do you want with it?" Xiaoman didn't say. He opened his notebook and, after "Xiaodou. Taihua.", added three more words: two thousand li.

exits.means: argues about the interest, refuses to own the debt

what.zh: 外门第一天，阿禾在小本子上记了你一笔：下下之资。你不认账——利息翻倍。
what.en: Your first day in the outer court: Ah He wrote you into the little notebook — bottom of the class. You disowned the debt, so the interest doubled.

story.zh:
小满道：「这也要算利息？」

阿禾道：「什么都要算利息。」她转身要走，走了两步，又回过头来，补了一句，「鸡蛋，三个半。别忘了。」

小满瞧着她那两截小辫子一跳一跳地走远了，心里头说不出是什么滋味。出门那天，老槐树底下只站着他娘一个人，他还道这丫头在睡懒觉。原来她早走了一天，走的是另一条路。

story.en:
"Even this earns interest?" said Xiaoman.

"Everything earns interest," said Ah He. She turned to go, took two steps, looked back and added, "Eggs: three and a half. Don't forget."

Xiaoman watched her two braids bob away and couldn't have said what he felt. The day he left, only his mother had stood under the old locust tree, and he'd thought this girl was sleeping in. She had left a day earlier, by another road.

For the next few days Xiaoman asked everyone the same thing: how far is Mount Taihua? Sun Ergou didn't know. An older disciple in the lecture hall overheard and laughed at him. "West. Two thousand li and more, in Yongzhou. The Taiyi Palace, up on Mount Taihua — the first sect under heaven. Their true disciples are precious; graze one's skin and somebody else takes the beating for him. What do you want with it?" Xiaoman didn't say. He opened his notebook and, after "Xiaodou. Taihua.", added three more words: two thousand li.
